\caption{\textbf{Under multiplicative fitness, the measured $V_A$ accounts for a small share of each observed deficit, and in most populations recurrent mutation maintains a small share of the measured $V_A$}. $\hat{V}_A$: posterior mode and 95\% HPD interval~\cite{bonnet2022}. Populations are grouped by mating system and listed by species and study site. $N_e/N$ at the posterior mode: the multiplicative model; the multiplicative bound; and their limit for small $V_A$, the small-variance approximation. $\log_{10}\hat{\delta}$: observed diversity relative to its neutral expectation at the census size, $\hat{\delta}$, on a log scale, where a diversity estimate and a census size are available (Methods); its reciprocal, $1/\hat{\delta}$, is the deficit. $V_A$ needed: the minimum variance that could account for $\hat{\delta}$. Shares, in percent, at the posterior mode and the point value of the direct mutation rate. Maintained: the share of $\hat{V}_A$ that recurrent mutation maintains at the assigned DFE, $U_d\bar{s}/\hat{V}_A$; values above 100 mean that mutation maintains all of it. Deficit: the share of the observed deficit that $\hat{V}_A$ accounts for under the multiplicative model, on a logarithmic scale, $\ln[1/(N_e/N)]/\ln(1/\hat{\delta})$.}
